description: Dispatch an async job that deletes up to 300 leads by id, and return {job_id, status} in milliseconds; poll check_marketo_job_status(job_id) for the finished results (per-record deleted/skipped status and reasons), row_count and tallies. Destructive write action — Marketo permanently removes the records.
embedding_description: Permanently remove lead records from Marketo's Lead Database by id, up to 300 per batch — a destructive, irreversible verb. Distinct from merge_leads (combines records into a winner rather than discarding them) and remove_leads_from_list (only removes list membership while the underlying lead record survives).

result_processor_customizations.result_description: Dict with job_id (pass to check_marketo_job_status) and status 'queued'. The completed job result is a dict with results (Marketo's per-record array: id, status [deleted/skipped], reasons on skip), row_count, and tallies (a status -> count summary).
result_processor_customizations.presentation_guidance: A queued job is not vendor success: give the job_id and poll check_marketo_job_status. Once completed, this destructive action's tallies must be surfaced clearly (e.g. '5 deleted, 1 skipped: lead not found') so the caller can confirm the intended leads were removed.
result_processor_customizations.output_action_guidance: Never say leads were deleted from THIS verb's response -- it carries only the job handle. Deletion is confirmed only once check_marketo_job_status reports status=completed.

error_processor_customizations.action_context: Validate a lead id batch and dispatch a background job that deletes those leads from the configured Marketo instance.
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: Refused at dispatch, before any vendor call and with no job created: marketo.invalid_params for missing/empty lead_ids, more than 300 ids, or missing session_id/flow_id in the calling context. Reported later in check_marketo_job_status's error field: marketo.not_configured: no marketo_instance address-book entry. marketo.auth_failed: OAuth credentials rejected. marketo.permission_denied: the API user's Role lacks Read-Write Person — this write permission is NOT checked by check_setup (unverifiable without performing a write), so this may be the FIRST signal of the gap. A transport fault after dispatch may follow a vendor mutation.
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: marketo.permission_denied: add 'Read-Write Person' under Admin > Users & Roles > Roles > <the API role> > Access API, then retry. Individual skipped records (e.g. lead not found) are in the results array, not an error. After a transport fault, confirm with get_leads which leads still exist before retrying.
